title: Matching records
description: Which records are the same thing: a copied bill and its original, one product or person under two entries.
metrics: Average precision over the candidate pairs
reliability: blocking's recall: the true pairs it keeps

question: Which decisions does DCLab reach on a matching records problem (Which records are the same thing: a copied bill and its original, one product or person under two entries), and do they hold?
hypothesis: Each decision a careful data scientist reaches on this kind of problem holds on every seed of the kind's replica.
setup_summary: The matching records kind's replica on seeds 0, 1, 2, brought as a person would; the five stages of the engine solve it, and each decision is checked on the finished run. No model is called.

claims.statement: Matching records: on 3 of 3 seeds every decision held (95% interval over seeds [0.439, 1.0]); 27 of 27 decision checks held.
limitations: Invented replicas with planted traps, three seeds: what the kind decides, not how well it does on real data.
Checks on one seed share its data, so they are not independent: the interval over seeds is the honest one.
